labelling_method: Hand-labelled from the rendered page text. This document is an Excel sheet printed to PDF: its reading order is scrambled (the header row is the last thing in the content stream), its rules are drawn as ~18,000 touching 0.72 pt squares, and it contains six live #REF! error values. The correct column count is judged from the x positions of the value tokens, which show two value columns per year (line items and subtotals sit at different x). Cells are given for a row range rather than the whole table where noted.

tables.note: Six columns: Particulars (the roman numeral is part of the label -- a seventh column for it is visually present but one row, 'Earnings per share (Basic and Diluted)', starts at the roman-numeral x and blocks any straight boundary), Note, then two value columns per year because subtotals sit at a different x from line items. The unit prints as '(` Million)': the grave accent is a rupee sign from a legacy font encoding, and reading it as INR must be a flagged inference.

reconciliation_expected.note: Total Expenses = the six expense line items above it

tables.labelling_correction: Corrected after metrics/eval.py flagged a disagreement: the first version of this label carried page 1's header ('As at March 31, 2023') onto page 2, which is the profit-and-loss statement and is headed '2022-23' / '2021-22'. The three header lines (y=68.7 '2022-23 2021-22', y=74.9 'Particulars Note', y=86.9 '( Million)') sit inside one row band at single line spacing, so this is ONE header row with wrapped cells, not two or three. Verified against the page token positions.
tables.labelling_correction_2: Corrected after metrics/eval.py flagged eight disagreements in column 1. The first version of this label gave the Note column numeric normalized values (25.0, 26.0, ...). That is wrong: '25' in a column headed 'Note' is a pointer to note 25, not a quantity, and typing it as a number invites a downstream consumer to sum it. The pipeline types the column 'reference' and leaves normalized_value null, which is the intended behaviour; the label was at fault.

structure_only.note: Balance sheet. Enumerators ('(a)', '(i)') occupy their own narrow column, the Note column is narrow with long labels beside it, and totals sit in a separate value column. Known-hard: the extractor merges the enumerator and Note columns into the label column. See LIMITATIONS.md L3.

value_expectations.note: Six of these exist in the cash-flow statement. They must never be coerced to 0 or to null-and-forgotten; a number the source document could not itself compute must not look like a number downstream.
